speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; please tell me, how long has this been happening and is it constant or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant traumatic event. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and is there any visible deformity to the finger now?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP and Lateral views) to rule out fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion fracture of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus at the distal phalanx).

The clinical picture of an inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the specific mechanism of injury where a finger is forcibly extended while the hand is closing, is classic for a ruptured flexor tendon. I have requested the X-rays to confirm if there is an associated avulsion fracture.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
